import sys


def main():
    flat = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()
    n = int(flat[0])
    turns = int(flat[1]) % 4  # four rotations restore the matrix
    del flat[:2]
    # ponytail: Python applies R^turns directly with C-level slices instead of cycling each
    # four-element orbit in place: R(r, c) = (c, n-1-r) for off-diagonal cells, diagonals fixed.
    # Tokens are re-emitted as read, so values are never converted.
    out = sys.stdout.buffer
    for i in range(n):
        if turns == 0:
            row = flat[i * n:(i + 1) * n]
        elif turns == 1:
            row = flat[i::n][::-1]  # column i read bottom to top
        elif turns == 2:
            row = flat[(n - 1 - i) * n:(n - i) * n][::-1]
        else:
            row = flat[n - 1 - i::n]  # column n-1-i read top to bottom
        row[i] = flat[i * n + i]  # both diagonals stay in place
        row[n - 1 - i] = flat[i * n + n - 1 - i]
        out.write(b" ".join(row))
        out.write(b"\n")


main()
